original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Kappa-blocker KB5, proof-level work on open problem F-star of research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7: cert(M) >= floor(2v/3) for every exact 3-total rational decoder. Three parts: (P1) PROVEN structural lemmas with exact hypotheses (support-forced anchor cert >= MAS(H) and cert = v when the block-incidence digraph is acyclic; matched-pivot certificate cert >= sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]) and cert = v when the zero digraph is 3-dichromatic; mod-2 anchor cert >= #{t : M_tt odd} in a 2-integral normalization), each demoted where unproved; (P2) independent stdlib reproduction of the one-copy L8 certificates on DreamingOfClouds' named instances tied_min (12 lines) and cex_min_1 (19 lines) of PR 2111, with exact cert values at tiny v and an exact chain-engine cross-check against PR 2111's stored cost-22 pairing; (P3) a targeted falsifier search beyond the censused domain of PR 2335 (v = 4..12, entries -2..2): factor entries in {-3..3} at v = 4..12 and v = 13..16 with tied-heavy 2-adic constructions, smallest v first, falsifier criterion an explicit admissible pairing B with sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j,A_j] < floor(2v/3) via the proven chain cert(M) <= cost(B).

Pair-collision check before computation (toolkit disc-comments on discussions 1317 and 1166 including nested replies, 2026-10-15 16:40 UTC) found no live F-star proof-level claim; the predecessor census https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335 is released. The handoffs thread's T = 3 open-core requests invite independent eyes on this exact object.
existing_restriction_being_changed: Nothing is relaxed. F-star is attacked as stated (floor form); the predecessor PR 2335 census's own limitation ('witnesses are lower bounds on cert, not a proof') is the restriction being addressed. Every lemma in the package carries its exact hypothesis, and every claim that is not proved is demoted to OPEN; no 'exactly when' or necessity wording is used without proof.
method: Exact stdlib integer/F2 arithmetic. Engine: for fixed a-labels the (b-labels, order, kept set) completion is exact by subset DP (b-exists is a per-line table lookup; f[T] = OR over t in T of f[T minus t] and b-exists(t, blockers of T minus t)); exact cert enumerates all a-labels at v <= 5; witness search hill-climbs over a-labels with exact completion; an independent witness checker replays every stored witness; falsifier criterion is an explicit admissible pairing B (0/1, unit diagonal, ones only where M vanishes) with chain cost sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j,A_j] < floor(2v/3), by the proven chain cost >= sum_j r_j >= cert(M). Controls: brute-force-over-all-labellings cross-check at v = 3, a hand-checkable diagonal decoder, corrupted-witness rejection, a matched-pivot witness constructed from MAS(H), and the chain engine recomputed on PR 2111's stored cost-22 pairing for cex_min_1.
parameter_ranges: T = 3 totals exactly; rational decoders M = sum_j p_j q_j^T with M_tt != 0. Named instances: PR 2111's tied_min (v = 12, entries in {-1,0,1}) and cex_min_1 (v = 19, entries in {-1,0,1}). Search beyond the censused domain of PR 2335: (i) factor entries in {-3..3} (outside the census alphabet {-2..2}) at v = 4..12, three instances per v; (ii) v = 13..16 (outside the census v-range) with entries in {-3..3} and tied-heavy 2-adic constructions (entries in {+-2,+-4} and {+-1,+-2}), two instances per v and family. Exact cert (exhaustive a-enumeration) at v = 5.

optimistic_full_cost_budget: No kappa, supplier, word or moment budget is in play (missing-lemma work). The whole-construction price is the evidence itself: every lemma proof is in the README and every computational claim is recomputed by verify.py in one bounded stdlib run (no third-party packages, no solver).
bottleneck_link: F-star is the named route to closing every open T = 3 window at once (research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7, consequence PROVEN given F-star): cost >= floor(2v/3) >= N(h) for every open T = 3 window. Proof-level structural lemmas narrow the remaining gap to exactly stated residue (isotropic/tied-minimum lines and non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs); a falsifier would redirect the T = 3 decoder route entirely.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact falsifier (smallest falsifying instance first: an explicit admissible B with cost below floor(2v/3), or exact cert below threshold at v <= 5), or, absent one, at the declared search domain with every instance witnessed at or above threshold and the exact obstruction recorded. One bounded pivot maximum; early kill with the exact obstruction recorded. Compute cap: about 90 minutes of single-process stdlib Python; each registered command below 600 seconds.
success_evidence: Written proofs of the structural lemmas (each demoted where incomplete) plus PASS markers from verify.py: engine/brute agreement at v = 3, the diagonal control, corrupted-witness rejection, the named-instance certificate reproduction (tied_min 11/12 and cex_min_1 18/19 machine-checked witnesses, matching PR 2111's recorded one-copy L8 maxima), exact cert values at v = 5, the chain engine recomputed on PR 2111's stored cost-22 pairing, structural lemma checks on every searched instance, and the declared-domain search summary with falsifier count.
falsification_test: Side A of the search is itself the falsifier test for F-star: an explicit admissible pairing B with cost(B) < floor(2v/3) refutes F-star (the chain cost >= cert(M) is proven). Side B witnesses are rejected by the independent checker if any K_tt = 1 fails or any before-pair constraint fails; corrupted copies of stored witnesses must fail verification (checked).
time_compute_cap: One session; compute capped at about 90 minutes single-process stdlib Python; no SAT solver, no third-party packages, no large downloads; each registered verify command capped at 600 seconds per the research_package.py limit.

PROVEN (written proofs in README.md): Lemma SF (support-forced incidences vanish: K_ts = 0 whenever pi(t) intersect sigma(s) is empty, hence cert(M) >= MAS(H), cert(M) = v for acyclic block-incidence digraph H, cert(M) >= v - fvs(H)); Lemma MP (matched-pivot certificate cert(M) >= sum_i MAS(Z[C_i]) for every pivot map into D(t), cert(M) = v when the zero digraph is 3-dichromatic with pivots in D(t)); Lemma RK (mutual-zero graph K4-free, zero digraph free of transitive 4-tournaments, no incidence with |pi(t) intersect sigma(s)| = 1); Lemma AN (mod-2 anchor: for 2-integral factorizations cert(M) >= #{t : M_tt odd}, so F-star holds for dyadic decoders with at most floor(v/3) even diagonals). CHECKED by verify.py (stdlib, deterministic, 17.7 s, certificate digest 134665ac6a0800e4): controls pass (brute-force-over-all-labellings agreement 3/3 at v = 3, diagonal control cert = 3, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2); named-instance one-copy L8 certificates of PR 2111 reproduced by a different stdlib-exact method — tied_min 11/12 (re-found by the deterministic search) and cex_min_1 18/19 (stored witness replayed), both exactly matching PR 2111's recorded CP-SAT maxima and both above floor(2v/3) = 8 and 12; PR 2111's stored cost-22 pairing for cex_min_1 recomputed exactly (chain cost 22 = 10+6+6, admissible) validating the chain engine; exact cert values by exhaustive a-enumeration: two v = 5 and one v = 6 instance, each cert = v exactly; structural lemma checks on 45 instances (mutual-zero K4-free and no transitive 4-tournament on 44 with v <= 16, matched-pivot witness replayed on 28 with v <= 12); beyond-census falsifier search: 43 instances (entries {-3..3} at v = 4..12, 27 instances; v = 13..16 entries3 8 instances; v = 13..16 tied-heavy 2-adic 8 instances), falsifiers = 0, minimum witness ratio 0.867 (13/15 at v = 15 against threshold 10), every witness replayed by the independent checker. NOT PROVED: F-star itself; the residue is stated exactly (tied-minimum/isotropic lines not covered by the anchor, zero digraphs that are not 3-dichromatic, non-dyadic entries); the B-search values are bounded-search upper bounds, not exact minima.

open_questions.question: Can the tied-minimum residue be ordered? Precisely: for lines whose diagonal cannot be anchored odd by any 2-integral normalization (the tied-minima obstruction of research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7), does there always exist an ordering and one-sided repairs keeping at least floor(2v/3) lines?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is exactly the residue left by the mod-2 anchor lemma: the anchor kills every incidence and leaves only unanchorable (isotropic) lines; a structure theorem for them would prove F-star.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate small tied-heavy decoders (entries in {+-2,+-4}, v <= 8) and classify the unanchorable lines by their valuation-tie type; test whether the anchorable count plus a greedy ordering of the tied classes always reaches floor(2v/3).
open_questions.blocked_by: No structural blocker; needs a dedicated enumeration session.

open_questions.question: Is every rank-3 decoder's zero digraph 3-dichromatic (partitionable into three acyclic classes, with pivots c(t) inside D(t) = pi(t) intersect sigma(t))?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The matched-pivot lemma would give cert(M) = v in that case; a counterexample would pin the exact combinatorial obstruction beyond the tied lines.
open_questions.first_step: Search decoders whose zero digraph has dichromatic number >= 4 (e.g. via cex_min_1 of PR 2111, whose cert = 18 < 19 forces it), and classify the minimal ones.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural; cex_min_1 already shows cert < v is possible, so the dichromatic question is genuinely open at the level of zero digraphs.

open_questions.question: What is the exact minimum of the chain cost sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j,A_j] over admissible pairings on tied_min and cex_min_1 (12 and 22 are the recorded values from PR 2111), and can the bounded B-search in verify.py be strengthened into an exact minimizer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An exact chain minimum pins cert(M) between the L8 certificate and the chain bound; on tied_min the recorded spread is 11 vs 12.
open_questions.first_step: Branch-and-bound over admissible pairings with the block-rank sum as the objective, seeded from PR 2111's stored cost-22 pairing on cex_min_1 and the 217 recorded optima structure on tied_min.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs a longer exact run than one session allows; the bounded search here records only upper bounds.
